entities.summary: The Encyclopedie, ou dictionnaire raisonne des sciences, des arts et des metiers (1751-1772), edited by Denis Diderot and Jean le Rond d'Alembert — the most ambitious reference work of the Enlightenment. Its 28 volumes compiled knowledge across all disciplines through a rationalist, secular lens, challenging religious authority and helping lay the intellectual groundwork for the French Revolution.
